item.title: Priest caught on CCTV sprinkling holy water on disputed fence as fight with neighbour escalates
item.description: A dispute over a metre-wide strip of land between a Russian Orthodox priest and his neighbour in West Yorkshire has escalated into police complaints, CCTV surveillance and criminal proceedings. The priest was also filmed sprinkling holy water near the disputed fence, which his wife described as an attempt to restore peace. With both households claiming ownership, the matter may now reach a civil court.

item.title: Gas Station Mass Shooting: Two killed, three hurt at West Baltimore BP; liquor store attack adds to toll
item.description: A tragic shooting occurred at a gas station in West Baltimore, claiming the lives of two individuals and leaving three others injured. Police arrived promptly to find multiple victims suffering from gunshot wounds. Investigations indicate that the attack may have been carried out by two or three assailants armed with high-powered rifles.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: $3.1 billion St. Louis data centre plan faces court fight over 120-MW project
item.description: St. Louis is undergoing a notable shift with the establishment of several data centres throughout the region. However, community members have voiced considerable opposition, raising health and environmental issues linked to these facilities. Legal actions have been launched by residents and developers encountering permit restrictions, leading to new legislation governing the operation and placement of data centres. Amidst this turmoil, national debates about AI infrastructure's effects on communities intensify.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kandinsky painting sold under Nazi occupation returns to heirs, fetches £31.56m at London auction
item.description: A remarkable Wassily Kandinsky painting achieved a staggering £31.56 million at auction, after being returned to the Lewenstein heirs. This valuable artwork had a tumultuous history, changing ownership during World War II amid sales disputes. Following an independent inquiry, it was restituted to the family, underscoring persistent endeavors to reclaim art stolen during the Nazi era.

item.title: At 7, she was 'gifted' to Queen Victoria; 176 years later, her descendant revisits her life
item.description: In 1850, a seven-year-old African girl named Aina was presented to Queen Victoria as a diplomatic 'gift' after losing her family and spending two years in captivity. Renamed Sarah Forbes Bonetta, she grew up under royal protection but faced restrictions on her freedom. Now, 176 years later, a new biography is examining her life, while her great-great-grandson, Bayo Randle, reflects on her struggles, achievements and complicated relationship with the British monarchy.

item.title: Camera giant Kodak operated a uranium-based nuclear device beneath its laboratory
item.description: For 31 years, Kodak operated a uranium-based research device beneath its Rochester laboratory, using it to examine materials and detect impurities. Installed in 1975 and shut down in 2006, the machine attracted public attention in 2012 because it contained highly enriched uranium. A new Popular Mechanics report explains how the device produced neutrons through nuclear fission but could not sustain a chain reaction independently, making it different from a conventional nuclear reactor.

item.title: Indian-origin couple spent over $100,000 to open cafe in Australia; an arson attack has them crodwfunding for repairs
item.description: Ashish Sharma and Manali Purohit's dream of running their vegan cafe 'And Bodega' in Fitzroy North, Melbourne, turned tragic when it suffered extensive damage from an arson attack shortly after opening. This incident, linked to a nearby tobacco shop, cost them their life savings and brought additional theft. To recover, they initiated a crowdfunding campaign and are searching for new locations, buoyed by the unwavering support of their community.

item.title: Flight Cleared After Bomb Alert: Bomb threat diverts Tel Aviv–Vienna flight; checks find no risk
item.description: Austrian Airlines flight OS82 faced a critical situation when it was diverted to Sofia due to a bomb threat. With 51 passengers on board, the plane made an emergency landing under the watch of a Bulgarian Air Force fighter jet. Upon arrival, security teams conducted extensive searches, finding no threats. The flight then continued its journey to Vienna later that night, ensuring the safety of all aboard.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: After two years living in a tent, Gaza potter built a clay dome home for his parents using earth and rubble
item.description: In the face of displacement from war, Jaafar Atallah crafted an innovative dome-shaped home from local clay for his family. Along with his community, he explored the potential of mud bricks, resulting in sturdier shelters compared to standard tents. This method emerges amidst Gaza's pressing housing crisis, driven by material shortages. Neighbors are also embracing recycled resources, ensuring traditional expertise evolves to tackle the region's housing emergency.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan to ban untreated firewood from January 2027 over risk of 140-plus pests and diseases
item.description: Michigan will ban untreated, uncertified firewood from entering the state starting January 1, 2027, to prevent the spread of more than 140 plant pests and diseases. The restriction will apply to travellers, campers and businesses, with exemptions for certified, heat-treated wood and certain other wood products. Authorities will focus on public awareness in 2027, while repeat violations could attract fines of $1,000 to $10,000 from 2028.

item.title: China’s economy gains pace on exports as domestic demand falters
item.description: In the July-September quarter, China recorded an economic growth of 4.5%, surpassing analysts' expectations. While exports showed strong performance, internal demand is tempering due to a sluggish property sector. The International Monetary Fund has projected a 4.5% growth rate for 2026, and Beijing aims for a 4.5%-5% growth this year. Meanwhile, trade imbalance concerns ignite dialogue among trading partners seeking sustainable solutions.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Women out of work, millions hungry: Afghanistan's lost 5 yrs under Taliban
item.description: Since the Taliban's resurgence in Afghanistan, women's rights and access to education have suffered dramatically. Millions of girls are now prohibited from secondary and higher education, leading to dire social repercussions. In addition, food insecurity is rampant, affecting approximately 19.2 million individuals. The healthcare available has also significantly declined, obstructing women's ability to obtain necessary medical assistance. The overall humanitarian crisis continues to worsen, deeply affecting Afghan families' daily lives.
